bug_semantics: The admin settings test_email action (app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb) takes params[:email] unvalidated, passes it to CamaleonCms::HtmlMailer.sender(params[:email], 'Test', data).deliver_now, and rescues SMTP failures with `render inline: e.message, status: 502`. Rails' render inline: feeds the string through ERB, so when an SMTP server rejects the crafted recipient the exception message (which embeds the attacker-controlled email address verbatim, e.g. `555 5.1.2 <%= ... %>: Recipient address rejected`) is evaluated as an ERB template on the server. An authenticated administrator (the endpoint requires :manage settings authorization) submits an email parameter containing ERB expressions; the SMTP rejection reflects it back inside e.message; the inline renderer evaluates the embedded Ruby, yielding arbitrary code execution as the Rails process user (CWE-1336).
flaw_origin: Commit 7dd48f47922526b5524b055c473d9c93a4cebcc6 ("admin: added button to send test emails \"smtp configuration\"", 2016-06-16, author Owen Peredo <owenperedo@gmail.com>; parent 298dc823fd2eff379c174ef239e571450d3562a4) first wrote the named sink: it created the test_email action in app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb with `CamaleonCms::HtmlMailer.sender(params[:email], 'Test', {content: 'Test content'}).deliver_now` and, on rescue, `render inline: e.message, status: 502` — the advisory's sink (attacker-controlled email reflected into an exception message rendered via ERB inline) is born here, together with the _email_settings.html.erb dialog and the routes/admin.rb entry that expose the parameter. The sink is a single line in a single commit; no later commit touched it before the fix.
ai_marker: absent — BIC author Owen Peredo <owenperedo@gmail.com> (human, repo owner), committer same, plain 2016 feature message; marker grep (claude/copilot/anthropic/openai/generated/co-authored/cursor/junie/manus) on 7dd48f47 returns no hits (NONE-7DD48F sentinel).
evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-73330 / GHSA-xgmr-hcvf-x3qc): CamaleonCMS 2.9.1 — SSTI in the test_email settings action; ERB tags in the email parameter are evaluated when an SMTP rejection reflects the recipient address back in the exception message rendered as an inline ERB template; authenticated admins achieve arbitrary command execution (CWE-1336).

BIC introduction: `git log -S 'render inline' -- app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb --format='%H %ad %an | %s' --date=short` returns exactly two commits: 7dd48f47 (2016-06-16, Owen Peredo, feature that adds test_email) and 092de84d (2026-04-26, the fix). `git show 7dd48f47:app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb` — :73 `def test_email`, :77-78 `rescue => e` / `render inline: e.message, status: 502`. The commit also adds the params[:email] call site (HtmlMailer.sender(params[:email], ...)), the _email_settings.html.erb dialog, and the config/routes/admin.rb entry.

Parent verification: `git show 7dd48f47 -s --format='%P'` → 298dc823fd2eff379c174ef239e571450d3562a4; `git show 298dc823:.../settings_controller.rb | grep -c 'render inline'` → 0 and `grep -c 'def test_email'` → 0 — the sink and the whole action are absent at the immediate parent (first-write confirmed).

Duplicate-commit check: a same-dated d46b4314be47089d8d384b9eb71546a3d0dd0343 ("admin: added button to send test emails...", 2016-06-16 13:19, parent fb685c46) touches only app/views/camaleon_cms/admin/settings/_email_settings.html.erb (1 insertion/1 deletion) — it does not touch the controller sink, so 7dd48f47 remains the first-write of the named sink. Both commits are human-authored with no AI markers (grep exit 1 on both).

Fix verification: 092de84dc706e3d6ed2e66e5c634092dc488fb69 (2026-04-26, author texpert <branzeanu.aurel@gmail.com>, "Fix SSTI vulnerability in test_email endpoint") replaces `render inline: e.message, status: 502` with `render plain: e.message, status: 502` in app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb and adds spec/requests/admin/settings/settings_controller_spec.rb; merged to mainline by 1b29de38434b03da04c674138023943dda94bb13 (Merge PR #1145, 2026-04-26). `git merge-base --is-ancestor 092de84d 2.9.2` → OK; `git tag --contains 092de84d` → 2.9.2, 2.9.3. Vulnerable state confirmed at advisory floor: `git show 2.9.1:.../settings_controller.rb` :72/:77 still has `render inline: e.message, status: 502`; fixed at 2.9.2 :80 `render plain: e.message, status: 502`; HEAD f89e2664 (2026-08-23) retains the plain: form.

Fix-completeness search: `git log --all -i --grep='ssti|test.email|73330|xgmr'` shows only the 092de84d fix, its merge 1b29de38, and unrelated 2016/2023 test-email commits — no other sink-touching commit exists.

Marker screening: NONE-7DD48F sentinel on the BIC (no AI trailers, no co-author lines; author=committer Owen Peredo). BIC-only attribution: fix-side commits carry no AI markers either (grep exit 1 on 092de84d and merge 1b29de38), so no AI signal anywhere in the lifecycle.

ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29 against clone history: git show 298dc823:app/controllers/camaleon_cms/admin/settings_controller.rb has 0 matches for test_email or 'render inline' (grep exit 1); the BIC 7dd48f47 adds the test_email action with HtmlMailer.sender(params[:email],...) and rescue => e; render inline: e.message. -> introducer_parent_absent=true.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory pins the sink precisely — ERB tags in the test_email email parameter, evaluated when the SMTP rejection message is rendered as an inline ERB template in CamaleonCMS 2.9.1. Code archaeology: `git log -S 'render inline'` on the controller yields exactly two commits, the 2016 feature commit 7dd48f47 and the 2026 fix 092de84d; 7dd48f47 is the first-write of both the params[:email] → HtmlMailer.sender call and the `render inline: e.message` rescue, and the whole action is absent at parent 298dc823 (verified by grep of the parent blob). A same-day duplicate commit d46b4314 was checked and only touches the view, not the sink. BIC = 7dd48f47, single-commit flaw, squash_decomposed=false. Tag cross-check: the BIC is contained from tag 2.3.1 onward and the vulnerable line persists verbatim at the advisory floor 2.9.1; the fix lands in 2.9.2/2.9.3, satisfying the affected-range and patched-boundary constraints. Fix: 092de84d is the direct mainline fix (reaches master via merge 1b29de384/PR #1145, so release-branch and mainline shas coincide — direct_fix_sha = fix_sha). AI decision: BIC-only attribution — the BIC object carries only human identity (Owen Peredo, 2016-06-16, a decade before the advisory) with no AI markers (NONE-7DD48F sentinel), so the verdict is NOT_AI; fix-side marker screening is likewise clean and is evidence-only regardless. The advisory's own CHANGELOG credit (PR #1145, reported by Amir Aliu and Enrik Mustafa) names human reporters, consistent with a human-authored, human-fixed decade-old design flaw.
